issue.description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift, VerifyReceipt(_:receipt:): runs the CLI's verify-receipt subcommand without --json and checks the result by trimming stdout and comparing to the literal string true.

This is inconsistent with every other method in this SDK, which all pass --json and decode a typed model, and it discards whatever detail the CLI might report about why a receipt failed verification (which of several checks failed, expected vs actual hash, etc) -- the caller only ever learns true or false.

Fix: pass --json to the verify-receipt invocation (assuming the pdftract CLI supports it there, same as extract/hash/classify) and decode a small structured result type (e.g. valid: Bool, reason: String?) instead of doing a raw string comparison on trimmed stdout.

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract); note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.

issue.description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift, both ExtractStream and Search: when a line from the CLI's NDJSON output fails JSON decoding, the catch block is empty except for a comment (// Skip malformed lines; the final error will be reported if needed / // Skip malformed lines) -- the line is dropped with zero signal to the caller.

Effect: a truncated write, a CLI bug emitting a malformed line, or a schema drift between the CLI and this SDK's Page/Match models all look identical to clean output that simply had fewer pages/matches than expected -- there's no way for a caller to distinguish silently-lost data from a PDF that genuinely had fewer results.

Fix: at minimum, surface a count of skipped/undecodable lines (e.g. via a side-channel callback, a final summary value, or by finishing the stream with a warning-carrying error type) instead of swallowing decode failures unconditionally.

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract); note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.
issue.title: Surface silently-dropped malformed JSON lines in ExtractStream/Search

issue.description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Types.swift, Source.bytes(let data) case in toArgs(): writes the PDF bytes to a new temp file under FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory (pdftract-input-UUID.pdf) so the CLI can read it, but nothing ever deletes that file afterward -- not in toArgs(), not in exec() after the process completes.

Effect: every call using Source.bytes(...) leaks one temp file per invocation, and for sensitive documents passed in-memory specifically to avoid touching disk, the PDF content ends up written to a shared temp directory anyway and stays there.

Fix: track the temp file path created in toArgs() and remove it after exec() (or the streaming equivalents) complete, including on the error path. Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Types.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract) to survive regeneration; note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.

issue.description:
README.md's Troubleshooting section states: The SDK will refuse to invoke mismatched binary versions. Install the correct version from the releases page.

There is no such check anywhere in the code. .codegen-version (currently 1.1.0) is never read at runtime by Sources/Pdftract or Sources/PdftractCodegen -- grep confirms no reference to codegen-version or any version-comparison logic in exec() or anywhere else. A user running an incompatible pdftract binary gets whatever error the mismatched CLI happens to produce, not a clear refuse-to-invoke message.

issue.description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift's private exec() (used by every non-streaming method: Extract, ExtractText, ExtractMarkdown, GetMetadata, Hash, Classify, VerifyReceipt) calls process.run() then process.waitUntilExit() BEFORE reading from outPipe/errPipe (the reads happen after waitUntilExit() returns).

If the pdftract CLI writes more JSON to stdout than the OS pipe buffer holds (typically 64KB on Linux) -- plausible for a multi-page or image-heavy PDF's --json output -- the child process blocks on write() because nothing is draining the pipe, while the parent is blocked in waitUntilExit() waiting for the child to exit. Classic Process/Pipe deadlock; the call hangs forever (or until a caller-imposed timeout external to this code kills it).

Note this repo's own ExtractStream and Search methods already read the pipe concurrently with the process running (readData(ofLength:) in a while process.isRunning loop) and do not have this bug -- exec() should use the same pattern: drain stdout/stderr concurrently (e.g. via a Task reading while waiting, or Pipe's readabilityHandler) rather than reading only after waitUntilExit().

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- do not edit manually. This needs to be fixed in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract) so it propagates on next regen; track that cross-repo dependency in this bead's resolution.
issue.title: Fix Process/Pipe deadlock risk in Methods.swift exec() for large PDF output

token fix on top of 6991c368/53daa014/6ea243eb from earlier this attempt):

disproved the assumptions the v1/v2 suites were built on and exposed THREE
real implementation gaps, each fixed through the generator templates (AC4):

1. FileHandle.readData(ofLength: 4096) on Linux Foundation loops until the
   full byte count or EOF (probe H: producer reached "read enter", never
   returned, stub's 3 lines sat in the pipe). The streaming producers now
   read availableData (one read()); values flow immediately.

2. AsyncThrowingStream fires onTermination ONLY for cancellation and
   producer finish; the producer task holds the continuation (the storage)
   alive for the child's whole lifetime, so break/drop can never be observed
   on the stream itself. Fix: the streaming methods return
   PdftractStream<Element>, a class AsyncSequence whose iterator deinit
   (loop exit, break included) and sequence deinit (drop before iterating)
   run the same idempotent terminate-only cleanup as onTermination; reaping

      claims the cleanup before handing out the iterator; only an unclaimed
      sequence release (true drop-before-iterate) runs the action; a
      producer that declines to launch finishes the stream.

Setup: clean extraction of HEAD 7dc0e749 at /tmp/pdfswift-verify-zKer (retained for diagnosis); docker swift:5.10-jammy; swift test --filter ExtractStreamConformanceTests. Binary: jedarden/pdftract Forgejo release v1.2.0 x86_64-unknown-linux-musl (sha256 f86d7274e89aa22d1faa13db8ab900344c4cd6fedc52e444094512f7d33152fa verified against release SHA256SUMS), mounted at /usr/local/bin/pdftract.

- testStreamedPageBlocksMatchExtract threw PdftractCodegen.CorruptPdfError: the generated client sends 'extract --json <input>' but the v1.2.0 CLI defines --json <PATH> (output path, '-' for stdout), so clap rejects the argv with exit 2 ('required arguments were not provided: <INPUT>') and the SDK exit-code table mislabels that as CorruptPdfError.
- extractStream is equally broken: CLI --ndjson emits per-BLOCK records {page, block_index, kind, bbox, spans}; the client decodes each line as Page (needs page_index/width/height/rotation/blocks), every line fails decoding and is silently dropped (onSkippedLine nil by default), so extractStream yields 0 pages and finishes cleanly. - testTrivialEmptyPdfYieldsZeroPages exposed an additional binary-side break: v1.2.0 exits 1 ('Document contains no pages') for a structurally valid zero-page PDF, where README/test expect an empty stream, not an error.

The test is correct: it failed against a real binary because the documented parity contract is genuinely broken in the generated client.

No file changes made here: the fix belongs in the pdftract Tera templates plus regeneration (editing generated code in this repo would be overwritten by the next codegen). Filed proposal for the protocol fix. Not closing: acceptance criterion 1 unmet.

issue.description:
All planned verification (bf-3fw, bf-25c) is compile/build-level; nothing provisions the pdftract binary the tests need or validates real output. README itself warns a mismatched binary 'may fail or return output that does not match this SDK's types'. Add a gate step (or explicit manual verification flow) that installs the pinned v1.1.0 release on the Linux runner and exercises extract, extractStream, search, getMetadata, hash, classify, and verifyReceipt against real PDFs, confirming stdout JSON parses into the Swift types without drift. This is the only check that catches serialization drift between codegen 1.1.0 and the binary.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.notes:
Release binary now exists: Forgejo release v1.2.0 (tag bf09c7dfede -> f4f6d6a8, canonical lineage) published with pdftract-v1.2.0-{x86_64,aarch64}-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz + SHA256SUMS (checksums verify; x86_64 binary runs, reports crate version 0.1.0); tag resolves on GitHub mirror (releases/tag/v1.2.0 HTTP 200 anon, ls-remote matches). HEADS-UP for the conformance run — template/CLI contract mismatch found while verifying the release: generated Methods.swift spawns valueless output flags ('extract <src> --json', '--text --json', '--md --json') but the pdftract CLI at BOTH f4f6d6a8 and the drop commit a2ed4c967 defines json/md/text as Vec<PathBuf> (value required, '-' for stdout) — 'extract t.pdf --json' exits 2 ('a value is required for --json <PATH>') on the released binary; CLI blocks are byte-identical across both lineages, so this predates the release and will fail ConformanceTests at the first extract call regardless of binary. Fix belongs to the codegen templates (emit '--json -' style) + regen drop, not to the release. No '-' insertion fallback exists anywhere in Methods.swift exec().

issue.close_reason:
Documented the pdftract binary discovery semantics in docs/notes/binary-discovery-semantics.md (commit fc40d4a7, pushed to origin/main — dc76bbda..fc40d4a7).

All four questions the bead asks are answered, from generated source plus an empirical probe (2026-11-25, swift:5.10-jammy, replicating the exact generated code path):

1. What the PATH search does: reads PATH (unset/empty -> no entries); splits on ":" on Linux only — the generated #else branch splits on ";" everywhere else, so on Apple platforms the whole PATH string becomes one candidate and discovery effectively never resolves (source-read, flagged unverified, no Apple host); empty entries dropped (PATH="a::b" verified: empty entry is NOT "current directory", unlike shell semantics); no ~ or variable expansion (~/pdftract verified failing X_OK); candidates "<entry>/pdftract" with relative entries resolved against CWD at scan time (verified PATH=relbin); acceptance = isExecutableFile (POSIX X_OK): 0755 file accepted, 0644 file skipped (deliberately — source comment), symlink-to-executable accepted, and a 0755 DIRECTORY named pdftract is accepted too (sharp edge documented: it then fails at spawn, NSCocoaErrorDomain 4, same localizedDescription text as not-found); first match in declared PATH order wins; memoized in a static let — at most once per process, thread-safe, negative result cached, so installing the binary mid-process never helps.
2. No environment-variable override exists: PATH is the only env var the SDK reads (sole environment[...] read in Sources/; CONFORMANCE_SUITE is test-only). binaryPath: is the only override mechanism; adding one would be an upstream Methods.swift.tera template change landing via codegen refresh.
3. Precedence: an explicit binaryPath: is stored verbatim with no init-time validation, and because the scan is a lazy static first touched only in the nil branch, an explicit path means the PATH scan never runs at all (not "runs and loses").
4. Not-found: init never throws; binaryPath falls back to the bare string "pdftract", which Foundation Process treats CWD-relative at spawn. Probe-verified: with an executable named pdftract in the process CWD, that file runs (exit 0 — CWD-hijack gotcha documented); otherwise the buffered methods throw the plain base PdftractError (not a subclass), exit code -1, message exactly "Failed to execute pdftract: The operation could not be completed. The file doesn’t exist." (underlying NSCocoaErrorDomain 260 / NSFileReadNoSuchFileError), matching the ExitCodeMappingTests lifecycle pin; extractStream/search finish the iteration by re-throwing the raw Foundation NSError unwrapped — NOT a PdftractError, so the README's own catch-as-PdftractError example misses it — matching the BinaryPathOverrideTests pin; nothing yielded, no hang.

Placement: docs/notes/ because README.md is one of the nine generated paths — an in-place README edit would be overwritten at the next codegen refresh; the doc states this and points upstream README wording changes at the jedarden/pdftract Tera templates (codegen-refresh.md workflow). Complements without duplicating pdfswift-30cb2045 (explicit-path API tests) and pdfswift-e83b1b91 (lifecycle-error tests), both cited as the pins this doc's claims rest on.

Checklist: (1) git status re-checked immediately before staging — committed only docs/notes/binary-discovery-semantics.md via a pathspec-scoped commit; another worker's in-flight edits (Methods/Types/three test files, untracked FlagLikeValuePassthroughTests.swift) and the staged .beads checkpoint deltas were neither included nor disturbed (git show --stat fc40d4a7 = exactly 1 file, +182). (2) Clean-extraction DoD: mktemp extraction of HEAD (fc40d4a7), scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast → "Build complete!", exit 0, extraction removed after success. (3) The bead names no explicit acceptance commands; the doc's behavioral claims were verified by the probe documented in the file. (4) Pushed; git rev-list origin/main..HEAD empty. No test/code changes, so no drift-gate or codegen surface touched.

issue.description:
The README documents the `.url(URL(...))` source and lists `SourceUnreachableError` (4), `RemoteFetchInterruptedError` (5), and `TlsError` (6), but nothing documents the actual fetch behavior those errors wrap: connect/read timeout values, whether redirects are followed (and how many hops), TLS verification strictness, proxy handling, and any response-size or content-type limits. Existing test beads (pdfswift-c84b293b, pdfswift-a53be3d4) cover that exit codes map to error types and that the APIs run — not the fetch semantics. Close the gap by capturing the pdftract CLI's URL-fetch behavior (verify against the real binary per pdfswift-3307a377), documenting it in the README near the `.url` example, and adding tests that pin the observable semantics (e.g., an unreachable host yields SourceUnreachableError, a bad certificate yields TlsError, an interrupted transfer yields RemoteFetchInterruptedError).

issue.description:
README.md now instructs `.package(url: ..., from: "1.2.0")` and points consumers at the pdftract v1.2.0 release, meaning the checked-in tree was regenerated against pdftract 1.2.0 — yet the only semver tag ever pushed is v1.1.0 (bf-4mw), and plan.md plus docs/notes/codegen-refresh.md still describe `.codegen-version` as 1.1.0. This recreates ADR-1's release-blocking defect at the new version: SwiftPM cannot resolve `from: "1.2.0"` until a matching tag exists on the canonical remote, and the docs contradict the README about which drop is shipped. Push a v1.2.0 annotated tag on the commit matching the regenerated tree, confirm it is reachable at the install URL consumers actually use (per pdfswift-63bde4de's canonical-URL decision), retarget the end-to-end binary verification (pdfswift-3307a377) at a real pdftract v1.2.0 binary rather than v1.1.0, and update plan.md / codegen-refresh.md's stated current version. Existing bead pdfswift-41fd9985 only *verifies* the install path; this bead is the fix that verification would otherwise trip over.

issue.description:
Split child 1 of umbrella pdfswift-6bc41168. Land the reworked regression-test watchdog currently sitting UNCOMMITTED in Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift.

Why the committed watchdog is insufficient: fef69c4 joins the consumer in a task group and calls cancelAll() on timeout. That cannot recover a real stderr backpressure deadlock — the consumer is blocked inside readData(ofLength:), cancelling it fires the stream's onTermination, and onTermination's process.terminate() + waitUntilExit() blocks too because the child is stuck in write() on a full stderr pipe. cancelAll() wedges and the suite hangs anyway.

The working tree already contains the replacement: the consumer runs detached, hands its DrainOutcome back through a DrainBox actor, the test polls the box instead of awaiting the consumer, and on timeout SIGKILLs the fake child via a pidfile the fake writes at startup (SIGKILL not SIGTERM — dash defers SIGTERM while blocked in write(); killing the shell, the only holder of the stdout write end, EOFs the deadlocked read and unwedges the run).

Scope: Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift ONLY. No production code changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- All four StreamingStderrRegressionTests cases route through the hardened drain(_:killChild:) harness.
- The timeout path SIGKILLs the fake child through its pidfile and fails an assertion instead of hanging the suite.
- The commit touches only Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift, is committed on main, and pushed to Forgejo origin (never github directly).

DONE. Policy decided and documented: SDK-only releases move the TAG, never the drop stamp.

The four --version-stamped sites (.codegen-version, README from:, README "generated against", README release link) name the pdftract drop, always. The release tag is the smallest unused X.Y.Z that is >= the drop stamp and shares its major.minor: equal on a drop-cut release (every release so far), one patch ahead for an SDK-only release (shim/fix work with no new drop). This publishes an SDK-only release without touching any generated file because SwiftPM from: is a floor — consumers resolve upward to the newest tag (float-up verified by the runbook's smoke check). Major/minor never diverge from the stamp (they track the generated lineage; shim-retirement majors coincide with a drop anyway); a patch drop colliding with a consumed SDK-only tag skips to the next free patch (never move a published tag).

The bead's floated alternative (bump README's from: and relax the consistency gate to a codegen-drop-prefix compare) is considered and REJECTED in the doc: it requires hand-editing generated output (drift, reverted next refresh, permanently red in the drift-gate byte-exact regen-and-diff) or regenerating at a fake --version (falsifies "generated against" provenance), and buys nothing since the floor semantics already reach the newer tag; a prefix-relaxed gate is also a weaker tripwire (cannot catch a stale single-site stamp; blurs the 0.1.0 rejection).

pdfswift-b2b1cd42 scoping resolved: it closed (commit 5d1ea8a3) before this policy existed, shipping the exact-equality gate across the four stamp sites plus the Package.swift no-literal tripwire. Under the tag-ahead policy that gate needs NO change — the feared conflict never materializes because an SDK-only release moves no stamp — and the drift gate's regen-and-diff needs no README exception, ever. Tag-vs-stamp stays a release-runbook check (gates extract trees, cannot see refs); the test's header comment now states the new relation.

issue.close_reason:
Documented the SDK's process-per-call execution model and its throughput implications in README.md (commit 2648f758, pushed to origin/main): new "Execution model" section between Cancellation/timeouts and Concurrency, cross-referenced from the Concurrency section's safety bullets. Covers all four points in the description:

1. One fresh pdftract child per call, buffered and streaming paths alike — no daemon, no connection reuse, no in-process engine. Verified against Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift (exec() and the streaming producer each construct a new Process() plus two pipes per call; the only shared state is the memoized PATH scan).

2. Per-call spawn latency, measured with the pinned v1.2.0 musl release binary on this 12-core Linux box: spawn+startup 0.5 ms median (n=50), extract 4-page/1.4 KB 1.3 ms (n=50), extract 1-page/6 MB 8 ms (n=20), extract 100-page/1 MB 330 ms (n=20). Documented as a table with the honest framing: fixed sub-millisecond term amortized to ~0.15% of a large extraction but ~40% of a trivial one; absolute numbers are machine-specific, the shape is the invariant.

3. Concurrent calls: no SDK-side limit — N calls become N simultaneous processes. Measured 16 concurrent 4-page extracts at ~5 ms wall vs ~24 ms serial (real parallelism, not serialization); documented memory scaling (~7 MB child RSS at startup, ~19 MB for the 100-page run, measured via wait4 ru_maxrss), the two-pipes-per-call fd cost, and that overload surfaces as kernel-killed children or spawn failures (exit -1) rather than a queue — callers must bound concurrency themselves.

4. When to prefer pdftract serve: verified upstream (crates/pdftract-cli/src/serve.rs + main.rs) that serve extracts in-process on a tokio blocking pool with rayon page parallelism (no fork/exec per request) behind a persistent shared on-disk cache (--cache-dir, --cache-size default 1 GiB, X-Pdftract-Cache hit/miss/skipped) that survives restarts. Verified the CLI cache is opt-in per invocation and the SDK never passes it (ExtractOptions has no cache field — checked Types.swift), so SDK calls are always cold extractions; the warm path exists only behind serve. Documented the trade-offs (no built-in auth/TLS/rate limiting, multipart instead of typed results) with cross-references to the existing Platform Support section, plus the explicit note that the SDK cannot talk to a serve instance (a .url source is fetched by the binary as PDF input).

Generator parity: same section mirrored into templates/sdk-skeleton/swift/README.md.tera in the local jedarden/pdftract lineage (commit 7384a927; lineage stays local per established practice — no push, push would be a lineage-landing event). Sections verified byte-identical between README.md and the template by diff.

Scope note: distinct from 2881ebed (iOS serve path — untouched), 215641c8 (Sendable/thread-safety — cross-linked, not duplicated), b64f41eb (cancellation/timeout — untouched).

issue.description:
No documented API bounds how long the subprocess may run or defines what happens when a consumer cancels the Task wrapping an in-flight extract/search or drops an extractStream sequence early. Cancellation must propagate to Process termination (kill + reap the child), an optional timeout should be available on exec(), and tests must prove a cancelled/dropped call does not leave an orphaned pdftract process or a caller blocked on a full Pipe. Document the resulting semantics in the README. Distinct from bf-um4 (which covers the stdout/stderr drain deadlock, not lifecycle).

issue.description: Proposal (discovered 2026-11-24 while pinning the buffered lifecycle error in pdfswift-e83b1b91, commit 30ea89dd). The buffered exec path wraps a Foundation spawn failure into PdftractError("Failed to execute pdftract: …", -1) (Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift:161), and ExitCodeMappingTests now pins that. The streaming producers do NOT wrap: their catch-alls re-throw the raw error via continuation.finish(throwing:) (Methods.swift:357, 485, 519, 644 — extractStream and search included), so a nonexistent or non-executable binaryPath on extractStream/search hands the caller a raw Foundation NSError that the README's own example (catch let error as PdftractError) would not catch, despite 'All methods ... can throw the following errors'. Fix belongs in the generator (Methods.swift.tera in jedarden/pdftract), not the generated tree, per docs/notes/codegen-refresh.md; the pdfswift-e83b1b91 tests deliberately do not pin the streaming spawn-failure path, since pinning current behavior would enshrine the drift. Proposed acceptance: after a regen refresh, extractStream/search with an unusable binaryPath finish by throwing the same wrapped lifecycle error the buffered path throws; extend ExitCodeMappingTests to pin both streaming paths then.

issue.description:
PROPOSAL (generated discovery from verification of pdfswift-23785038 - needs explicit admission, do not self-approve).

The generated Swift client (Sources/PdftractCodegen, codegen-version 1.2.0) cannot drive any released pdftract binary: all binary-facing methods are non-functional. Demonstrated against pdftract v1.2.0 (musl, sha256 f86d7274) with the real-binary conformance run recorded on pdfswift-23785038:

1. extract/extractText/extractMarkdown argv: client sends 'extract --json <input>' / '<input> --text --json'; the CLI defines --json/--md/--text as value-taking output paths ('-' = stdout). Every call dies as a clap usage error (exit 2), which the SDK exit table mislabels CorruptPdfError. Correct stdout shape is 'extract --json - <input>' (verified working).
2. JSON schema: CLI page object is {blocks, index, spans, tables}, blocks {bbox, kind, spans, text}; generated Page requires page_index/width/height/rotation/spans/blocks. Document decoding fails even after the argv fix.
3. extractStream: CLI --ndjson emits per-block records {page, block_index, kind, bbox, spans}; the client decodes lines as Page, so every line is silently dropped and the stream yields 0 pages. Parity between extract() and extractStream() (README contract, ExtractStreamConformanceTests) is untestable until this is fixed.
4. Zero-page PDFs: CLI exits 1 'Document contains no pages' for a structurally valid 0-page PDF; README/test expect an empty stream.

Fix belongs in jedarden/pdftract templates/sdk-skeleton/swift/*.tera (Methods.swift.tera argv + Types.swift.tera schema) AND a CLI-side page-level NDJSON wire format - pdftract-core already has the header/page/footer frame protocol (crates/pdftract-core/src/output/ndjson/frames.rs + pipeline.rs) but it is wired only to the Python bindings, never to the CLI. Decide the canonical wire protocol, wire it into the CLI (or realign the templates to block records), fix zero-page handling, regenerate pdftract-swift via 'pdftract sdk codegen', validate with 'pdftract sdk validate', then re-run the ExtractStreamConformanceTests verification on pdfswift-23785038 against a real binary - that bead stays open until this lands.

AND the debug build (~/pdftract @ a2ed4c96): zero-page PDF (Count 0, Kids []) exits 1 'Document contains no pages' on both 'extract --json -' and 'extract --ndjson'; --ndjson emits per-block records; client extractStream yields 0 pages for multi-page fixtures; extract() dies as CorruptPdfError. Full run output recorded on pdfswift-01c3eebb.

Human-approved 2026-10-03. Downstream owner only: consume the canonical upstream repair from pdftract/pdftract-29a848db, regenerate the Swift SDK, and prove buffered extraction, page-stream ordering/schema parity, empty-document behavior, and real-binary conformance. Do not invent a Swift-only block-grouping protocol.

issue.description:
README's extractStream and search examples iterate with plain `for await`, while the error-handling section states all methods are `async throws`. As written the examples either fail to compile (if the sequences are throwing AsyncSequences) or, if they are non-throwing, there is no documented way for a mid-stream failure (exit codes 2-6) to reach the caller. Verify which shape Methods.swift actually emits, correct the examples, and add a short note on how errors surface from the streaming APIs. README is generator output, so the fix must land in jedarden/pdftract's Swift templates and be regenerated (same fix-upstream-then-regenerate flow as bf-1b5) — a hand-edit would be reverted by the next refresh.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.notes:
Verified shape and implemented. Methods.swift:354/515: extractStream returns AsyncThrowingStream<Page, Error>, search returns AsyncThrowingStream<Match, Error> — plain for-await does not compile; both README examples corrected to for try await. Error propagation confirmed in code: pre-output failures (toArgs/spawn) finish(throwing:) before any value; on child exit != 0 the producer reaps, drains stderr, and finish(throwing: mapError(stderr, status)) AFTER yielding everything decoded — so already-emitted values arrive first, then the mapped error throws at stream end; undecodable lines go to onSkippedLine, never thrown. New README section 'Errors from the streaming methods' documents all three behaviors.

VERDICT: the ranged-GET read deadline is ~10 s TOTAL-TIME-based (not idle-gap), but firing it never stops the process — the identical ranged GET is re-issued indefinitely, so any GET whose body takes longer than ~10 s total (stalled OR legitimately slow) hangs pdftract extract with empty stderr until externally killed. There is NO effective process-level read/stall timeout; observed minimum hang = the 90 s probe cap (exit 124, 8 identical GET attempts logged server-side, no backoff/escalation).

1. Probe 1 http://127.0.0.1:18765/slow/body/15000 (15 s mid-body stall; HEAD answered instantly): wall 90004 ms, exit 124 (external 90 s cap), stderr EMPTY. Server log: HEAD + 8 identical ranged GETs (Range: bytes=0-65535) at +10.13/+10.24 s spacing until kill.
2. Probe 2 /trickle/20 is not runnable against this client — wall 7 ms, exit 1, stderr verbatim: 'Error: Failed to download remote PDF / Caused by: Server does not support Range requests' (route answers 200, no Accept-Ranges; server.py: only /ok.pdf, /slow/connect, /slow/body, /slow/rangestall, /rangetrickle are 206-capable). Ran its purpose-built 206-capable twin /rangetrickle/20 (1 byte/100 ms for 20 s total): wall 90003 ms, exit 124 (external cap), stderr EMPTY, 8 identical GETs at +10.00/+10.01 s spacing. Continuous 100 ms data flow still cut at 10.0 s per attempt ⇒ TOTAL-TIME semantics, NOT idle-gap (an idle/read timeout would have completed at ~20 s).
3. Probe 3 http://127.0.0.1:18765/hang (never responds): wall 10243 ms, exit 1, stderr verbatim: 'Error: Failed to open remote PDF source / Caused by: HEAD request failed: request timeout'. Cut by the client's own ~10 s deadline (not the 90 s cap, not the 120 s server cap); exactly one HEAD, no retry. Observed minimum no-response hang: 10.2 s.
4. Probe 4 (TLS row, standing ruling verbatim): TLS unusable with self-signed; timeout not observable. Fresh corroboration: https://127.0.0.1:18443/slow/body/15000 → 7 ms, exit 1, 'HEAD request failed: connection interrupted' (https /ok.pdf identical: 8 ms). Read-stall phase over TLS is unreachable — the handshake fails first, so HTTP and HTTPS are not comparable on this harness.
5. Sub-deadline control /slow/body/5000: wall 5016 ms, exit 0, stderr empty, exactly one GET — stalls under ~10 s total succeed cleanly; brackets the deadline from below (consistent with child 2's 8 s TTFB control). Baseline /ok.pdf 55 ms exit 0.
MECHANISM (v1.2.0 source, ~/scratch/pdfswift-1d763709/probe-tmp/pdftract-v120-src): crates/pdftract-core/src/source/http_range.rs:26 CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS=10 (misnamed — overall request deadline) applied at :132 as ureq AgentBuilder::timeout on the agent used for BOTH HEAD and ranged GETs; ureq 2.12.1 agent timeout spans request start through body read ⇒ total-time. fetch_range (:297) maps body-read failure to io::ErrorKind::Interrupted ('Failed to read response body'); read_range/read/prefetch have no retry loop — the endless identical GETs are the upstream std Interrupted-retry idiom (Read::read_exact ignores ErrorKind::Interrupted) colliding with the per-request deadline. READ_TIMEOUT_SECS=30 (:29, :722) belongs to the NON-range fallback full-download path, not this one. Fix shape for a future bead: non-Interrupted error kind or bounded escalating retry, and a true idle/read timeout separate from the overall deadline. Full evidence + verbatim stderr on this bead's notes; raw artifacts ~/scratch/pdfswift-1d763709/probe-tmp/ (read-phase-probes.sh, read-probes.txt, read-stderr/, /tmp/probe-http.jsonl slices); durable doc write is child 4's job.

DONE. Policy decided and documented: SDK-only releases move the TAG, never the drop stamp.

The four --version-stamped sites (.codegen-version, README from:, README "generated against", README release link) name the pdftract drop, always. The release tag is the smallest unused X.Y.Z that is >= the drop stamp and shares its major.minor: equal on a drop-cut release (every release so far), one patch ahead for an SDK-only release (shim/fix work with no new drop). This publishes an SDK-only release without touching any generated file because SwiftPM from: is a floor — consumers resolve upward to the newest tag (float-up verified by the runbook's smoke check). Major/minor never diverge from the stamp (they track the generated lineage; shim-retirement majors coincide with a drop anyway); a patch drop colliding with a consumed SDK-only tag skips to the next free patch (never move a published tag).

The bead's floated alternative (bump README's from: and relax the consistency gate to a codegen-drop-prefix compare) is considered and REJECTED in the doc: it requires hand-editing generated output (drift, reverted next refresh, permanently red in the drift-gate byte-exact regen-and-diff) or regenerating at a fake --version (falsifies "generated against" provenance), and buys nothing since the floor semantics already reach the newer tag; a prefix-relaxed gate is also a weaker tripwire (cannot catch a stale single-site stamp; blurs the 0.1.0 rejection).
